newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Emperor warns of higher gold mine costs.
newsitem.headline: Emperor warns of higher gold mine costs.

text.p: Emperor Mines Ltd said on Monday that the 1996/97 (July-June) financial year was a challenging one for its Vatukoula mine in Fiji, with lower-than-expected production resulting in higher unit cash costs.

However, Emperor said it has hedged in forward sales markets over four years worth of gold production, or 36 percent of total reserves, enabling it to sustain low gold prices for a longer period than some other Australian mining companies.
The industry average is only 2.5 years worth of hedging, Emperor said.
A total of 540,000 ounces of gold is sold forward by Emperor at a rate of 20,000 ounces a quarter ending in March 2004 at a price of US$421.20 an ounce, it said.
This equates to about A$565 an ounce, Emperor added.
Gold currently fetches about US$320 an ounce, or A$435 an ounce.

Despite a record 140,000 tonnes of ore being treated in April and May at the Vatukoula mine, performances have been affected by problems associated with the new crushing circuit, which will impact on Emperor achieving its production of 140,000 ounces for the financial year, the miner said earlier this year.
Cash costs in the third quarter averaged A$486 an ounce, which was up 16.3 percent from the previous quarter, Emperor reported in April.
As production now moves to a higher capacity of 200,000 ounces and new mechanised mining techniques are employed, cash costs in the current year should come down significantly, the company said.
